shortcut_name: Treating conflict logs as an unordered graph
evidence: gpt-oss-120b uses an "adjacency matrix for O(1) edge test" and "adjacency bitsets"; qwen3-coder builds "adj[u].add(v)" and says "For each edge (u,v), look for a common neighbor w". Both discard input-log order.
affordance_in_statement: Each report involves exactly two technicians who refuse to operate on the same shift. ... a trio of distinct technicians where each technician in the trio has a logged conflict with the other two technicians.
removal_suggestion: Make log position semantically relevant: require the three pair reports for a qualifying trio to occur in three consecutive input lines, while retaining the same lexicographic tie-break. The examples already place their intended three reports first and consecutively.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Converts all reports into unordered adjacency structures and tests pairwise connectivity, ignoring report order.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Each report involves exactly two technicians who refuse to operate on the same shift.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Stores reports in sets, sorts the undirected edges, and searches for a common neighbor; this also ignores the order in which reports are logged.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: a trio of distinct technicians where each technician in the trio has a logged conflict with the other two technicians

common_affordance: Interpreting the m conflict reports solely as an unordered undirected edge set, with no significance attached to their input-log order

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The implementation performs an essentially cubic search over vertex triples and did not complete successfully under the resource limits.
It explicitly iterates through all possible ordered triples, producing cubic-time work at n up to 2000 and timing out.

recommended_edit: Add to the trio definition: "The three conflict reports for the trio must occupy three consecutive lines of the input." Require the lexicographically smallest trio among those satisfying both pairwise-conflict and consecutiveness conditions.
